rows.title: Deep Learning Model for Automated Segmentation of Orbital Structures in MRI Images.
rows.method: Self-configuring nnU-Net CNN with five-fold cross-validation
rows.dataset: private cohort (117 patients with orbital pathologies)
rows.metric_values: Mean DSC: ocular bulb 0.931; optic nerve 0.820; ocular tumors 0.788; retinal detachment 0.550. Detection ROC AUC: ocular tumors 0.90; retinal detachment 0.78.
rows.summary: nnU-Net automated segmentation of four orbital structures, achieving strongest performance for the ocular bulb and optic nerve while tumor and retinal detachment segmentation remained challenging.

rows.title: Automated segmentation of pituitary adenomas, pituitary gland, and internal carotid arteries on routine coronal contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI: a single-sequence feasibility study.
rows.method: Swin-Unet transformer and self-configuring nnU-Net CNN, with five-fold cross-validation and ensemble predictions
rows.dataset: private cohort (255 patients with surgically confirmed pituitary adenomas)
rows.metric_values: Swin-Unet vs nnU-Net: mean DSC 0.70 (95% CI 0.66–0.74) vs 0.69 (0.65–0.73); mean HD95 5.21 mm (95% CI 4.40–6.03) vs 5.30 mm (4.44–6.16); mean slice-level F1 0.89 ± 0.09 vs 0.87 ± 0.08. Mean computation time 78.4 seconds/patient (95% CI 61.5–95.5).
rows.summary: Swin-Unet and nnU-Net demonstrated comparable feasibility for segmenting pituitary adenomas, the pituitary gland, and internal carotid arteries using a single routine MRI sequence.

rows.title: Self-configuring nnU-net pipeline enables fully automatic infarct segmentation in late enhancement MRI after myocardial infarction.
rows.method: Self-configuring nnU-Net using phase-sensitive inversion recovery, magnitude reconstruction, or both as inputs
rows.dataset: private cohort (170 examinations from 78 patients; evaluation subset of 10 patients)
rows.metric_values: PSIR and MAG: mean DSC 0.83 ± 0.03 for myocardium and 0.72 ± 0.08 for scars; infarct-volume Pearson r = 0.96.
rows.summary: nnU-Net automatically segmented myocardium and infarct tissue with strong agreement with manual delineation, although infarct volumes were significantly underestimated.

rows.title: Automatic segmentation for magnetic resonance imaging guided individual elective lymph node irradiation in head and neck cancer patients.
rows.journal: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
rows.method: 3D nnU-Net CNN with transfer learning for adaptation to another medical center
rows.dataset: private cohort (50 UMC-Utrecht HNSCC patients: 40 training and 10 testing; 20 additional patients from another center)
rows.metric_values: Median DSC 0.72; recall 0.76; precision 0.78; F1-score 0.78; recall higher than both observers (p = 0.002).
rows.summary: nnU-Net segmented individual elective lymph nodes with higher detection recall than manual observers and required retraining for successful transfer to another center.

rows.title: Evaluation of deep learning models for segmentation of hippocampus volumes from MRI images in Alzheimer's disease.
rows.method: Comparison of U-Net, YOLO-v8, and DeepLab-v3
rows.dataset: Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI): 300 subjects, including 100 AD, 100 MCI, and 100 normal controls; 7,859 image slices
rows.metric_values: U-Net IoU: AD 0.639; MCI 0.801; normal controls 0.751. YOLO-v8 IoU: AD 0.342; MCI 0.465; normal controls 0.550.
rows.summary: The study compared three deep learning models for bilateral hippocampus segmentation on ADNI MRI and found U-Net performed best across diagnostic groups.

rows.title: An improved 3D-UNet-based brain hippocampus segmentation model based on MR images.
rows.method: Improved 3D-UNet incorporating a filling technique and data augmentation, compared with VNet, SegResNet, UNetR, and original networks
rows.dataset: private cohort (200 images from Hangzhou Cancer Hospital: 145 training, 30 hyperparameter tuning, and 25 testing)
rows.summary: Adding a filling technique improved hippocampus segmentation across multiple networks, with the modified 3D-UNet achieving the best reported performance.

rows.title: Automated Brain Tissue Segmentation on CT guided by MRI: Advancing AI‐based Neuroimaging for Dementia
rows.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
rows.method: 2D and 3D nnU-Net and 3D MedNeXt trained with MRI-derived labels for CT segmentation
rows.modality: Brain CT with paired MRI-derived supervision
rows.dataset: Gothenburg H70 Birth Cohort (N = 733); National University Hospital Singapore Memory Clinic Cohort / NUS Dementia Cohort (N = 210)
rows.metric_values: Average DSC, axial/coronal/sagittal: 3D nnU-Net 0.82/0.72/0.76; MedNeXt 0.83/0.73/0.78. MedNeXt volumetric similarity 0.842–0.992. Dementia cohorts: MedNeXt average DSC 0.73 and volumetric similarity 0.912; nnU-Net 0.70 and 0.854.
rows.summary: MRI-guided training enabled CT segmentation of gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid, with MedNeXt achieving higher accuracy and dementia-cohort generalizability than nnU-Net.

rows.title: Deep Learning for Automated Ventricle and Periventricular Space Segmentation on CT and T1CE MRI in Neuro-Oncology Patients.
rows.method: nnU-Net ventricle segmentation compared with pretrained SynthSeg
rows.modality: CT and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted brain MRI
rows.dataset: private cohort (78 patients for training; internal and external test sets of 18 patients each)
rows.summary: nnU-Net enabled ventricle and derived periventricular-space delineation, outperforming SynthSeg on internal segmentation metrics and receiving better clinical ratings on both test sets.

rows.title: Evaluating Traditional, Deep Learning and Subfield Methods for Automatically Segmenting the Hippocampus From MRI.
rows.method: Comparative evaluation of FreeSurfer, SynthSeg, FastSurfer, FIRST, e2dhipseg, Hippmapper, Hippodeep, FreeSurfer-Subfields, HippUnfold, and HSF
rows.dataset: not stated (three datasets with manually segmented hippocampus labels)
rows.summary: An independent comparison of ten hippocampus segmentation methods found greater errors on clinical data and frequent anterior oversegmentation, highlighting the need for more diverse manually labeled datasets.

rows.title: LI-RADS-based hepatocellular carcinoma risk mapping using contrast-enhanced MRI and self-configuring deep learning.
rows.journal: Cancer imaging : the official publication of the International Cancer Imaging Society
rows.method: Ensemble of nnU-Net semantic segmentation models with 14 input channels and post-processing for lesion detection and LI-RADS classification
rows.dataset: private cohort (602 patients: 383 training and 219 internal testing); modified LiverHccSeg dataset (16 external-test patients)
rows.metric_values: Training/internal/external cohorts, lesions ≥10 mm: sensitivity 0.41–0.85/0.40–0.90/0.83; PPV 0.70–0.94/0.67–0.88/0.90; classification F1 0.48–0.69/0.47–0.74/0.84; median per-lesion Dice 0.61–0.74/0.52–0.77/0.84. LR-5 specifically: sensitivity 0.85/0.90/0.83; PPV 0.94/0.88/0.90; F1 0.69/0.74/0.84; Dice 0.74/0.77/0.84.
rows.summary: An nnU-Net ensemble generated LI-RADS tumor risk maps from contrast-enhanced MRI with strong LR-5 detection, while automatic LI-RADS classification required further improvement.
